sanskrit: ut tiṣṭhaiva parehīto ajñāte kim ihecchasi | grīvās te kṛtye pādau ca- -api kartsyāmi nir drava ||
english: Rise up and begone, O sorcery-charm dispatched by an unknown one — what do you seek here? I shall cut off your neck and feet, O kṛtya; flee away!

sanskrit: indrāgnī asmān rakṣatāṃ yau prajānāṃ prajāpatī | somo rājādhipā mṛḍitā ca- -ṛtasya naḥ patayo mṛḍayantu ||
english: May Indra and Agni, the two lords of creatures, protect us; may Soma the king, the supreme sovereign who bestows grace, and the lords of cosmic order be gracious to us.

sanskrit: bhavāśarvāv asyatāṃ pāpakṛtvane kṛtyākṛte duṣkṛte vidyutaṃ devahetim ||
english: Let Bhava and Śarva hurl the divine lightning-bolt of the gods against the evil-doer, against the maker of the kṛtya, against the worker of ill.

sanskrit: yady eyatha dvipadī catuṣpadī kṛtyākṛtā saṃbhṛtā viśvarūpā | seto 'ṣṭāpadī bhūtvā punaḥ parehi ducchune ||
english: Whether you have come as a two-footed or four-footed kṛtya, assembled and fashioned in all forms by the sorcerer — having become an eight-footed beast of ill omen, go back the way you came!

sanskrit: abhyaktāktā svaraṃkṛtā sarvaṃ bharantī duritaṃ parehi | jānīhi kṛtye kartāraṃ duhiteva pitaraṃ svam ||
english: Smeared and anointed, arrayed in her own cry, carrying all evil — begone! Seek out, O kṛtya, your maker, as a daughter seeks her own father.

sanskrit: parehi kṛtye mā tiṣṭho viddhasyeva padaṃ naya | mṛgaḥ sa mṛgayus tvaṃ na tvā nikartum arhati ||
english: Begone, O kṛtya, do not linger — lead back your step as if to one who has been pierced. He is the quarry and you the hunter; he who sent you does not deserve to destroy you.

sanskrit: martyo mṛtyuḥ svayaṃkṛtaṃ yaṃ cakārācittyā | hastābhyām ātmane vadham ||
english: The mortal is his own death — he who, through heedlessness, fashioned with his own two hands destruction for himself.

sanskrit: uta hanti pūrvāsinaṃ pratyādāyāpara iṣvā | uto pūrvasya nighnato vi hanty aparaḥ prati ||
english: The later one smites with his arrow the one who sat before, having reclaimed it; and in turn the later one strikes back against the one who is slaying the former.

sanskrit: etad dhi śṛṇu me vaco athehi yata eyatha | yas tvā cakāra taṃ punaḥ ||
english: Hear this word of mine and return to where you came from; go back again to the one who fashioned you.

sanskrit: anāgohatyaṃ vai bhīmaṃ kṛtye mā no gām aśvaṃ puruṣaṃ vadhīḥ ||
english: The slaying of the innocent is truly dreadful, O kṛtya; do not smite our cow, our horse, our man.

sanskrit: yatrayatrāsi nihitā tatas tvotthāpayāmasi | parṇāl laghīyasī bhava ||
english: Wherever you have been deposited, from there we rouse you up and drive you forth; become lighter than a leaf.

sanskrit: yadi stha tamasāvṛtā jālenābhihitā yūyam | sarvāḥ saṃlupyetaḥ kṛtyāḥ punaḥ kartre pra hiṇmasi ||
english: If you are shrouded in darkness, covered over with a net — we dissolve you all, O kṛtyās, and send you back again to the maker.

sanskrit: kṛtyākṛtaṃ mūlakṛtam abhiniṣkāriṇaḥ prajām | mṛṇīhi kṛtye moc chiṣo amuṃ kṛtyākṛtaṃ jahi ||
english: Crush the offspring of the one who has gone forth, who made the kṛtya, who performed root-sorcery; O kṛtya, do not spare him — smite yonder maker of the kṛtya!

sanskrit: yathā sūryas tamaso mucyate pari rātriṃ jahāty uṣasaś ca ketūn | evāhaṃ sarvaṃ durbhūtaṃ hastīva rajo duritaṃ jahāmi ||
english: As the sun is freed from darkness, casts off the night, and surpasses the beacons of dawn — so I cast off all ill-being and evil, as an elephant shakes off dust.

sanskrit: upamitaḥ pratimito 'tho parimitaś ca yāḥ | śālāyā viśvavārāyā naddhāni vi cṛtāmasi ||
english: The ties that are measured at the top, measured across, and measured around — the knottings of the all-sheltering house we now unloose.

sanskrit: yat te naddhaṃ viśvavāre pāśo granthiś ca yaḥ kṛtaḥ | bṛhaspatir ivāhaṃ balaṃ vācā vi sraṃsayāmi tat ||
english: Whatever noose has been bound in you, O all-sheltering one, and whatever knot has been made — I, like Bṛhaspati, undo that binding by the power of the sacred word.

sanskrit: ā yayāma saṃ babarha granthiṃ cakāra te dṛḍham | parūṃṣi vidvāṃ śasteva- -indreṇa vi cṛtāmasi ||
english: He who drew tight, who compacted and made a firm knot in you — knowing your joints, we loosen them as if with a blade, together with Indra.

sanskrit: saṃdaṃśānāṃ paladānāṃ pariṣvañjalyasya ca | sarvā mānasya patnyā te naddhāni vi cṛtāmasi ||
english: The knottings of the clamps, of the peg-fastenings, and of the encircling embrace — all the bindings of yours, O wife of the house-lord, we now unloose.

sanskrit: vaṃśānāṃ te nahanāni prāṇāhasya tṛṇasya ca | pakṣāṇāṃ viśvavāre te naddhāni vi cṛtāmasi ||
english: The lashings of your bamboo rafters, and of the binding-grass, and of the wing-beams — all your bindings, O all-sheltering house, we now unloose.

sanskrit: yāni te antaḥ śikyāny ābedhū raṇyāya kam | pra te tāni vi cṛtāmasi śivā mānasya patni na uddhitā tanve bhava ||
english: The hanging nets within you that they have pierced through for some purpose — those we now loosen for you. Be auspicious, O wife of the house-lord; do not afflict the body with what is unbound.

sanskrit: havirdhānam agniśālaṃ patnīnāṃ sadanaṃ sadaḥ | sado devānām asi devi śāle ||
english: The hall of the oblation-press, the fire-shed, the seat and dwelling of the wives — you are the seat of the gods, O divine house.

sanskrit: akṣum opaśaṃ vitataṃ sahasrākṣaṃ viṣūvati | apinaddham abhihitaṃ brahmaṇā vi cṛtāmasi ||
english: The axle-pin, the peg, what is spread wide, what is thousand-eyed and turned on all sides — what is fastened and bound down we now unloose by means of sacred speech.

sanskrit: yaś ca tvā prati gṛhṇāti yena cāsi mitā tvam | ubhau mānasya patni tau jīvatāṃ jaradaṣṭī ||
english: He who receives you in his keeping and he by whose effort you have been built — both of them, O wife of the house-lord, may they live to old age.

sanskrit: amutrainam ā gacchatād dṛḍhā naddhā pariṣkṛtā | tasyās te vi cṛtāmasy aṅgamaṅgaṃ paruṣparuḥ ||
english: Let her who is firm, well-bound, and fully adorned go to meet him there — of her, we unloose you limb from limb, joint by joint.
